audit.why: 53.08% over 699 games supports a Camille-sided chart at every stage, with first item flagged as the one even window because Purgatory arrives to answer the Ultimatum. No stage needed moving.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one ability of his is named outside Purgatory, and no spike carries a cooldown, so 'force his R first' and 'Hookshot engages off cooldown' have no clock. Ritual Nails is 10/9/8/7/6s, Soul Ignition 18/17/16/15/14s, Ashen Pursuit a flat 10s, Purgatory 120/100/80s.
audit.why: Cooldowns from champ-data/_kits/locke.json. Purgatory's 120s at rank 1 is the number that makes the first-item stage even and the rest of the map yours - it is the whole reason 'force his R first' is worth doing.
audit.corrected: spikes[3].text, mid and whys[5] now carry Purgatory's 120s; early names the Silver Stake on-hit scaling.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction is absent: Purgatory denies your mobility outright - both Hookshot and The Hextech Ultimatum - rather than merely 'trading a totem for your Ultimatum'. Two more were missing: Soul Ignition (W) hurts him up front and then heals back a portion of what he took, so it is a delayed heal you can pre-empt with Grievous Wounds; and Silver Stake (P) is on-hit magic damage that grows with your MISSING health, so his damage climbs exactly as the fight goes on. Purgatory also executes. Camille's Hookshot is called a stun; Riot's text says knock-up.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json for camille vs locke: 'Locke can deny your mobility (Hookshot (E), The Hextech Ultimatum (R)) with Purgatory (R)', 'Locke sustains through chip damage (Soul Ignition (W))', 'Locke threatens a threshold kill with Purgatory (R)'. Riot: Silver Stake - 'Locke's attacks deal additional magic damage On-Hit, increased based on enemy missing Health.' Soul Ignition - 'dealing damage to himself. At the end of the duration, Locke will heal back a portion of the damage he takes.'
audit.corrected: spikes[3].text, mid, late, early and whys[5] now say Purgatory denies the dash rather than trades with it, name the execute, name the Silver Stake missing-health scaling, and put Grievous Wounds on Soul Ignition.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal call, despite Soul Ignition being his only sustain and the reason a won trade can be refunded.
audit.why: Soul Ignition front-loads self-damage and pays it back as a heal at the end of the duration - Grievous Wounds applied during the window is what stops the refund.
audit.corrected: mid now buys Grievous Wounds and times it to the Soul Ignition window.

edits.before: Two-plus items the isolation game is yours: Ultimatum cages him away from help, Hookshot reaches him over terrain, and true damage doesn't care what he builds. Hunt the pick in the sidelane, dive him under tower with R zoning the pixel he stands on, and end fights before they begin.
edits.after: Two-plus items the isolation game is yours: Ultimatum cages him away from help, Hookshot reaches him over terrain, and true damage doesn't care what he builds. Hunt the pick in the sidelane and dive under tower — but never step in with Purgatory up, because grounded you have no dash at all.

notes: The one thing that decides this matchup was written as a fair trade: Purgatory does not swap a totem for your Ultimatum, it GROUNDS you, and grounded Camille has neither Hookshot nor the Ultimatum dash - she is a melee bruiser with no gap-close. _missing-interactions.json lists exactly that for this pairing. Silver Stake scaling with the TARGET's missing health is the other thing a player needs and never had: it means the longer he keeps you low the harder he hits, which inverts the usual 'I'm ahead on HP so I can extend' instinct. This entry's wants.you and wants.foe strings are 21-31 characters, so the +/-10% band leaves no room to add anything - they stay as bare labels. _missing-interactions also claims your Hookshot shuts off his Ashen Pursuit; I did not write that, because nothing in either kit description explains the mechanism and I will not ship a dash-denial a player would commit an all-in on.
